option.value: {"D:/AGH/Semestr III/Programowanie obiektowe/Labs/PO_2023_PON1500_ADAMCZYK":"{\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/WorldElement.java\":\"This file defines an interface called WorldElement in the agh.ics.oop.model package.\\n\\nAn interface in Java defines a contract that classes can implement to provide common functionality. This WorldElement interface is likely being used to define common properties and methods for different types of \\\"world elements\\\" or objects that can exist in a game or simulation world.\\n\\nThe key functions defined in the WorldElement interface are:\\n\\n- getPosition() - Returns the position of the world element as a Vector2d object. This allows any implementing class to have a 2D position.\\n\\n- toString() - Defines a toString() method that implementing classes must provide to convert the object to a String representation. This is commonly used for debugging or logging.\\n\\nSo in summary, this interface:\\n\\n- Defines a common \\\"contract\\\" for world elements in a 2D world \\n- Specifies they have a 2D position\\n- Requires a string representation\\n\\nClasses that implement WorldElement can then be used polymorphically where only the interface is needed, rather than a specific class. This promotes code reuse and flexibility.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MapDirection.java\":\"This file defines an enum called MapDirection that represents the four cardinal directions (North, East, South, West) that can be used on a 2D map.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- toString() - Returns a single character string representation of the direction (\\\"N\\\", \\\"S\\\", \\\"E\\\", \\\"W\\\")\\n\\n- next() - Returns the direction that comes after this one in a clockwise order \\n\\n- previous() - Returns the direction that comes before this one in a clockwise order\\n\\n- toUnitVector() - Returns a Vector2d object representing the direction as a unit vector (0,1) for North, (1,0) for East, etc. \\n\\nSo in summary, it defines an enum for directions and provides useful methods to work with directions like getting the next/previous one, converting to a string or vector representation. This would be useful for any application that needs to represent and work with cardinal directions on a 2D grid or map.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/Grass.java\":\"This Java file defines a Grass class that represents grass elements in a 2D world simulation.\\n\\nKey points:\\n\\n- The Grass class implements the WorldElement interface, indicating it represents an element that can exist in the world.\\n\\n- It has a Vector2d position field to store the x,y coordinates of the grass.\\n\\n- The constructor takes a Vector2d and assigns it to the position field. \\n\\n- getPosition() returns the grass\\u0027 position Vector2d.\\n\\n- toString() overrides the default toString and returns \\\"*\\\" to represent grass visually when printed.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- Constructor - Initializes a new Grass instance with a given position\\n- getPosition() - Gets the Vector2d position of the grass\\n- toString() - Defines the string representation of grass as \\\"*\\\"\\n\\nSo in summary, this Grass class defines a basic grass element for a 2D world simulation with its position and string representation. It implements the necessary WorldElement interface.\",\"/oolab/src/test/java/agh/ics/oop/model/Vector2dTest.java\":\"This file contains unit tests for the Vector2d class.\\n\\nThe key things it does:\\n\\n- Defines a Vector2dTest class that extends the JUnit test class\\n- Contains a series of test methods annotated with @Test\\n- Creates Vector2d objects to pass to the methods being tested\\n- Uses JUnit assertions like assertEquals to validate the results\\n\\nThe key functions/methods it tests include:\\n\\n- equals() - tests vector equality \\n- toString() - tests string representation\\n- precedes() - tests vector ordering\\n- follows() - tests reverse vector ordering\\n- upperRight() - tests finding the upper right vector\\n- lowerLeft() - tests finding the lower left vector\\n- add() - tests vector addition\\n- subtract() - tests vector subtraction \\n- opposite() - tests getting the opposite vector\\n\\nSo in summary, it defines a set of unit tests to validate the core functionality of the Vector2d class like equality, ordering, arithmetic operations, etc. Using JUnit it runs the tests and ensures the class behaves as expected.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MoveValidator.java\":\"This file defines an interface called MoveValidator in the agh.ics.oop.model package.\\n\\nThe MoveValidator interface:\\n\\n- Defines a validation method called canMoveTo() that takes a Vector2d position as a parameter.\\n\\n- Specifies that canMoveTo() returns a boolean indicating whether an object can move to the given position.\\n\\nSo in summary, this interface:\\n\\n- Defines a contract for classes that validate whether objects can move to certain positions.\\n\\n- Classes that implement MoveValidator must implement the canMoveTo() method to perform the validation logic. \\n\\n- Other classes can then use a MoveValidator to check if moves are valid by calling canMoveTo() and passing in a proposed new position.\\n\\nThe key function defined in this interface is:\\n\\n- canMoveTo(Vector2d position) - Validates if an object can move to the given position, returning a boolean.\\n\\nSo this interface allows classes to validate object movements in a two-dimensional space represented by Vector2d coordinates.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/WorldMap.java\":\"This file defines an interface called WorldMap that is responsible for interacting with the map of the world in a game.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- place(Animal animal) - Places an animal on the map if the move is valid.\\n\\n- move(Animal animal, MoveDirection direction) - Moves an animal on the map in the specified direction, if the move is possible. \\n\\n- isOccupied(Vector2d position) - Checks if a position on the map is occupied.\\n\\n- objectAt(Vector2d position) - Returns the WorldElement at a given position, or null if unoccupied. \\n\\n- getElements() - Returns a collection of all WorldElements on the map.\\n\\nThe WorldMap interface extends the MoveValidator interface, implying it will also implement functions related to validating moves. Overall, it provides functions for placing/moving objects on the map, checking map positions, and accessing the map elements. This allows interaction with and querying of the game world map.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/AbstractWorldMap.java\":\"This file defines an abstract base class called AbstractWorldMap that implements the WorldMap interface. It provides a basic implementation of a 2D world map that can contain animals.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- getLowerLeft() and getUpperRight() - Abstract methods that subclasses must implement to define the boundaries of the map.\\n\\n- animals - A HashMap that stores the animals placed on the map, mapped by their position. \\n\\n- place(Animal) - Adds an animal to the map at its position if space is available.\\n\\n- move(Animal, direction) - Moves an animal in a given direction by updating its position in the animals map. \\n\\n- isOccupied(position) - Checks if a position is occupied by an animal.\\n\\n- objectAt(position) - Returns the animal occupying a position, or null if empty.\\n\\n- toString() - Renders the map as a string using a MapVisualizer class.\\n\\nSo in summary, it provides a basic implementation of a 2D map that can store animals in positions, allow placing/moving animals, and check for occupied spaces. Subclasses would define the specific map boundaries and properties.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/OptionsParser.java\":\"This OptionsParser file is used to parse command line arguments into a list of MoveDirection enum values.\\n\\nThe key things it does:\\n\\n- It is in the agh.ics.oop package\\n- It has a static parse method that takes a String array of arguments\\n- The parse method creates a LinkedList to store the parsed MoveDirection values\\n- It loops through the arguments and uses a switch statement to map single character args to MoveDirection enums \\n- \\\"f\\\" maps to FORWARD, \\\"b\\\" maps to BACKWARD, \\\"r\\\" maps to RIGHT, \\\"l\\\" maps to LEFT\\n- It adds the parsed MoveDirection to the LinkedList\\n- The LinkedList of MoveDirection values is returned\\n\\nSo in summary, it takes command line arguments and parses them into a list of MoveDirection enum values to represent robot movement directions. The key function is the static parse method.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MapVisualizer.java\":\"This file defines the MapVisualizer class which is used to convert a WorldMap object into a string representation that can be printed.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- draw(lowerLeft, upperRight) - Takes coordinates of the region to draw and returns a string representation of that region of the map\\n\\n- drawHeader() - Generates the header row with x/y labels \\n\\n- drawFrame() - Draws the frame segments around cells\\n\\n- drawObject() - Draws the object at a given position, or empty cell if none\\n\\nThe draw method loops through the region, calls the other drawing methods to generate each row as a string, and returns the full map region as a single string that can then be printed. \\n\\nSo in summary, it takes a WorldMap object and converts it to a printable string representation of a selected region, by handling the cell framing, headers, and drawing of objects in each cell.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/Animal.java\":\"This file defines an Animal class that represents an animal in the simulation world.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- Constructor - Initializes the animal\\u0027s position and map direction.\\n\\n- getMapDirection/setMapDirection - Get/set the direction the animal is facing on the map.\\n\\n- getPosition/setPosition - Get/set the animal\\u0027s position on the map. \\n\\n- toString - Returns a string representation of the animal\\u0027s facing direction.\\n\\n- isAt - Checks if the animal is at a given position.\\n\\n- moveForward/moveBackward - Moves the animal in its facing direction or opposite direction if valid.\\n\\n- move - Changes the animal\\u0027s facing direction or moves it forward/backward based on the passed MoveDirection. Validates the move using a MoveValidator.\\n\\nSo in summary, it defines the core properties and behaviors of an animal entity in the simulation - its position, facing direction, and ability to move/change direction on the map if valid according to a move validator.\",\"/oolab/src/test/java/agh/ics/oop/model/RectangularMapTest.java\":\"This file contains unit tests for the RectangularMap class.\\n\\nThe key things it does:\\n\\n- Defines a RectangularMapTest class to hold the test methods\\n- Imports the necessary classes for testing (JUnit, RectangularMap, etc)\\n\\nThe key test methods are:\\n\\n- testPlaceAndObjectAt() - Tests placing an object on the map and retrieving it\\n- testMove() - Tests moving an object on the map \\n- testIsOccupied() - Tests checking if a position is occupied\\n\\nThe tests:\\n\\n- Set up a RectangularMap and Animal object\\n- Perform the operation being tested (place, move, check occupancy)\\n- Assert that the expected results occurred\\n\\nSo in summary, it:\\n\\n- Sets up JUnit tests\\n- Creates sample data (map and object)\\n- Exercises key RectangularMap methods \\n- Verifies the methods work as expected through assertions\\n\\nThis allows testing the core functionality of the RectangularMap class in isolation.\",\"/oolab/src/test/java/agh/ics/oop/IntegrationTest.java\":\"This file contains integration tests for the simulation model.\\n\\nKey things it does:\\n\\n- Imports the necessary classes from the simulation package (Simulation, model classes etc)\\n- Defines test methods annotated with @Test\\n- Sets up simulations with different configurations - single animal, multiple animals, collisions, blocked movement\\n- Runs the simulations\\n- Asserts that the final state of the simulation matches the expected state - positions, orientations of objects\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- testSimulationSingleAnimal() - Tests a simple simulation with one animal\\n- testSimulationMultipleAnimals() - Tests with multiple animals \\n- testSimulationWithCollision() - Tests collision handling\\n- testSimulationBlockedMovement() - Tests blocked movement at map boundaries\\n\\nThe tests set up Simulation objects with different configurations, run the simulations, and then validate the final state matches expectations. This helps test that the core simulation logic is working as intended when integrating different components and scenarios.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MoveDirection.java\":\"This MoveDirection.java file defines an enum called MoveDirection that represents different directions an object can move in a 2D space.\\n\\nThe key things it does:\\n\\n- Defines the possible direction values as enum constants - FORWARD, BACKWARD, RIGHT, LEFT\\n\\n- Has a toUnitVector() method that converts each direction to a unit vector representation as a Vector2d object. This allows easy conversion from a direction to a vector that can be used for things like moving an object.\\n\\n- The toUnitVector() method uses a switch expression to return the appropriate Vector2d for each direction:\\n - FORWARD returns (0, 1) \\n - BACKWARD returns (0, -1)\\n - RIGHT returns (1, 0)\\n - LEFT returns (-1, 0)\\n\\nSo in summary, it provides an enum to represent common movement directions, and a way to convert those directions to unit vectors for actually applying movement in a 2D space. This encapsulates the direction logic in one place and allows other code to easily work with directions.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/GrassField.java\":\"This GrassField class represents a grass field world map in the simulation.\\n\\nKey things it does:\\n\\n- Extends AbstractWorldMap to inherit common world map functionality\\n- Stores a list of Grass objects that populate the field\\n- Constructor takes a grass count and places that many Grass objects randomly on the field\\n- placeGrass() method handles randomly positioning and adding each Grass\\n- objectAt() returns the WorldElement (Grass or Animal) at a given position\\n- getElements() returns the list of Grass objects \\n- getLowerLeft/getUpperRight calculate the bounding box of elements\\n- canMoveTo checks if a position is occupied and if so, if by an Animal\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- Constructor to initialize field with grass\\n- placeGrass() to randomly position and add grass\\n- objectAt() to get element at a position \\n- getElements() to get list of grass\\n- Bounding box calculation methods\\n- canMoveTo() to check if a move is valid\\n\\nSo in summary, it represents a grass field for the simulation, initializes grass randomly, and provides methods to interact with elements on the field.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/World.java\":\"This Java file defines the main World class that acts as the entry point for the simulation program.\\n\\nKey things it does:\\n\\n- Defines the main() method, which is the starting point of execution.\\n\\n- Parses command line arguments into a list of MoveDirection using OptionsParser.\\n\\n- Creates a list of starting positions as Vector2d objects. \\n\\n- Creates a WorldMap instance using the GrassField implementation.\\n\\n- Initializes a Simulation object, passing in the positions, directions and map. \\n\\n- Runs the simulation by calling simulation.run().\\n\\n- Prints start and stop messages.\\n\\nKey functions/classes:\\n\\n- main() - Entry point\\n- OptionsParser - Parses command line args \\n- Vector2d - Represents 2D positions\\n- WorldMap - Interface for map types\\n- GrassField - Concrete map implementation\\n- Simulation - Core simulation class\\n\\nSo in summary, it sets up the required objects for the simulation and kicks off the main simulation loop by calling run() on the Simulation instance.\",\"/oolab/src/test/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MapDirectionTest.java\":\"This file contains unit tests for the MapDirection enum class.\\n\\nKey things it does:\\n\\n- Defines two test methods - testNext() and testPrevious()\\n- testNext() asserts the next direction returned after calling next() on each direction \\n- It checks that calling next() sequentially cycles through the directions correctly\\n- testPrevious() does the same but for the previous() method\\n- It asserts the previous direction returned after calling previous() on each direction\\n- Again checking it cycles through the directions correctly going backwards\\n\\nThe key functions/methods it tests are:\\n\\n- MapDirection.next() - Returns the next direction in the cycle \\n- MapDirection.previous() - Returns the previous direction in the cycle\\n\\nIt uses JUnit assertions (assertEquals) to verify the expected direction is returned after calling next() or previous() on each MapDirection value.\\n\\nThis allows testing that the MapDirection enum behaves as expected when cycling through the directions with next() and previous(). It validates the core functionality of the enum.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/Simulation.java\":\"This file defines a Simulation class that simulates the movement of animals on a world map.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- Constructor: Initializes the simulation by taking in the initial animal positions, list of move directions, and world map. Creates Animal objects and adds them to the animals list.\\n\\n- getAnimals(): Returns the list of Animal objects being simulated. \\n\\n- getMoves(): Returns the list of move directions for each step.\\n\\n- getMap(): Returns the world map object.\\n\\n- run(): Runs a single simulation by iterating through the move directions list and moving each animal according to the direction. Prints the map after each move.\\n\\n- run(): An overloaded version that also tracks and returns the actual move directions and positions of each animal at each step. This allows observing the simulation in more detail. \\n\\n- It uses the world map object to place animals initially and move them according to directions. The map tracks animal positions and prevents overlapping.\\n\\nSo in summary, it sets up and runs a simulation of animal movement on a map according to predefined move directions, optionally tracking detailed movement data. The world map manages animal placement and movement.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/Vector2d.java\":\"This file defines a Vector2d class that represents a 2D vector/point with x and y coordinates.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- Constructor that takes x and y values\\n- Getter methods for x and y \\n- toString() method to return a string representation of the vector\\n- precedes() and follows() methods to compare vector positions\\n- add(), subtract() methods to perform vector math operations \\n- upperRight(), lowerLeft() methods to find bounding box vectors\\n- opposite() method to invert the vector\\n- equals() and hashCode() methods to support object equality comparisons\\n\\nSo in summary, it defines a basic 2D vector class with common vector operations like addition, subtraction, comparisons, and string representation. This allows representing and manipulating 2D points/vectors in code using this class.\",\"/oolab/src/main/java/agh/ics/oop/model/RectangularMap.java\":\"This file defines a RectangularMap class that implements the WorldMap interface. It represents a rectangular 2D map with animals placed on it.\\n\\nKey functions:\\n\\n- place(Animal animal) - Places an animal on the map if the position is unoccupied.\\n\\n- move(Animal animal, MoveDirection direction) - Moves an animal in the given direction if the new position is valid. Removes and re-adds the animal to the internal map.\\n\\n- isOccupied(Vector2d position) - Checks if a position is occupied by an animal. \\n\\n- objectAt(Vector2d position) - Gets the animal/object at a given position.\\n\\n- getElements() - Gets all animals on the map as a list.\\n\\n- canMoveTo(Vector2d position) - Checks if an animal can move to the given position based on map boundaries. \\n\\n- toString() - Returns a string representation of the map by calling the MapVisualizer class.\\n\\nThe key data structure is a HashMap that maps positions (Vector2d) to animals to track their locations on the map. It implements the basic functionality for placing and moving animals on a rectangular grid-based map.\",\"/oolab/src/test/java/agh/ics/oop/model/MapIntegrationTest.java\":\"This file contains integration tests for the Map and GrassField classes.\\n\\nKey things it does:\\n\\n- Sets up a RectangularMap and GrassField before each test, with some default dimensions and grass count.\\n\\n- Initializes an Animal object with a known position.\\n\\n- Tests the place() method on both maps to ensure the animal can be placed.\\n\\n- Tests the isOccupied() method to check if the known position is marked as occupied after placing the animal. \\n\\n- Tests the objectAt() method to retrieve the animal object from the known position.\\n\\n- Adds an additional test for objectAt() to check it returns an object of the expected type (Animal).\\n\\nKey functions tested:\\n\\n- Map.place() - Places an object on the map\\n- Map.isOccupied() - Checks if a position is occupied \\n- Map.objectAt() - Gets the object at a position\\n\\nThis helps validate the core functionality of placing and retrieving objects on different map types works as expected when integrated together.\",\"/README.md\":\"This README.md file provides information about a Git project or repository.\\n\\nThe key things it includes are:\\n\\n1.
